acceptance: VERIFY: Tests: a head with a would-block verdict and no baseline change is refused with a message naming the step and the baseline file; a head with the baseline updated arms; a clean head arms; a missing verdict is reported and does not block (report-only phase)
VERIFY: Dry run against a real PR head with a pass verdict arms normally (run recorded)
GUARDRAIL: Refusal never bypasses or substitutes for core; no new label, comment or environment-variable override; remote arming targets apply the same rule
context:
DONE 2026-10-26: PR #3536 merged as 64dfb3563e6445d32166b5adceb0f9ad9e2fcf47 (oracle SHIP on d594f670). ci.yml's verify step writes fast-duration-verdict.json, uploaded as fast-duration-verdict-<pr>-<headsha> (overwrite, 14d). scripts/pr_arm.py duration_verdict_refusals (also wired into scripts/remote_closeout.py) refuses arming on a current-head would-block verdict — message names both ratios, the measurement item and the baseline script — unless the PR changes tests/fixtures/fast_tier_baseline/; pass/neutral/rejected/missing arm normally; stale-head verdicts ignored; unreadable file list fails closed. Demonstrated live on PR #3536 ('verdict for d594f670a is pass; arming is not held'); 245 preflight tests pass. Post-merge Trunk 40290210452 success.

Source: CI time-regression incident of 2026-10-25 and an independent adversarial review of the prevention plan. PR #3423 added an autouse module-scoped fixture (tests/conftest.py, _chdb_connections_closed_after_module) that opened a chDB probe session after every module; the fast-tier pytest time went from 327.81 s (run 40143597290) to 1041.10 s (run 40195371347) and PR CI wall time from about 12 to 20+ minutes for about 18 hours before anyone noticed. No CI check measured test time: _project/scripts/fast_lane_ceiling_check.py checks marker composition only, and tests/duration_policy.py's per-test T1 budget is refreshed from nightly data and never sees module-teardown cost spread across tests. Pre-incident fast-job wall time varied 7.8-18.0 min (cv about 19%), so job wall time cannot be a blocking signal; summed per-test junit time is the blocking metric.
description: Last-line defense during report-only mode and for changes outside pytest. scripts/pr_arm.py (make pr-arm and remote arming) reads the PR head's verify-fast-duration verdict from core's output and refuses to arm when it reported a would-block verdict and the PR does not change the baseline file. It does not re-measure job durations (too noisy). Trigger regardless of paths; the verdict already reflects the change.
